introH2: 🏖️ What are Bophut & Fisherman’s Village like, and which zone fits your trip?
introHtml: If Chaweng is the loudest, brightest side of Koh Samui, Bophut on the island’s north coast is almost the opposite — a quiet beach under the coconut palms, shallow water that pulls far out at low tide, and an old fishing village at its heart that everyone calls Fisherman’s Village. Its old seafront lane is lined with weathered wooden shophouses turned into restaurants, bars, cafés and gift shops, and it fills with people after dark — especially the famous Friday Walking Street night market. · The charm of Bophut is getting a quiet beach and a walkable eat-and-drink strip in one place, all just about 10 minutes from Samui airport — which makes it work for your first night, last night, or a long stay. · But the stays here give genuinely different trips — right on the sand you get quiet and sea views; in the middle of the walking street you can stroll to food and beach but hear the nightlife after dark; and set back in a garden you get the most privacy and shade. Book the wrong zone and the mood of the trip changes. · This guide gathers 8 Bophut & Fisherman’s Village hotels we have already reviewed in depth across every price level — each drawn from reading real guest reviews, with honest highs and caveats, prices compared across 3 sites, and direct booking links.
mrtHtml: Koh Samui has no rail transit — you get around by hotel car, taxi, Grab, or a rented scooter/car. · Bophut sits on the island’s north coast, only about 10 minutes from Samui airport (USM) and roughly 10–15 minutes by car from Chaweng. · The stay zones in this guide: Bophut beachfront — on the sand or a few steps away, quiet with sea views (Hansar, NH Collection Peace, Zazen, The Waterfront) · Heart of Fisherman’s Village — on the walking street, a few minutes’ walk to food and beach, cheaper, but you hear the nightlife at night (Dreamcatcher, Hacienda) · Quiet end of the village — the far seafront end, close enough to walk out but calm after dark (GREENLIGHT) · In a tropical garden — set back from the lane, the shadiest and most private, a few minutes’ walk to the village (Anantara Bophut) · Bophut is a shallow beach, so if you plan to swim, check the tide times or hop over to Chaweng now and then.

entries.storyHtml: If you want a luxury beachfront resort you can still walk out of and into the fishing village in two minutes, Hansar Samui Resort & Spa is the most complete answer in Bophut — a right-sized 5-star resort of just 74 rooms, sitting directly on Bophut Beach yet only a couple of minutes from the old lane and night market of Fisherman’s Village. It scores 9.1 from 967 reviews on Booking.com. · What real guest reviews agree on: every room faces the sea, rooms run a generous ~50 sqm with big balconies, teak floors and terrazzo bathrooms, plus a beachfront saltwater infinity pool, the Luxsa Spa, and service so many guests name as the highlight of the trip — staff who remember your name and genuinely look after you. · Honest caveats: Bophut is a quiet beach where the water pulls far out at low tide and some days brings natural seaweed — it is not the wide white sand of Chaweng; the resort has been open for years and a few rooms show their age; peak-season rates run high and in-resort food and drink are priced like a 5-star. · Best for couples and honeymooners who want beachfront luxury without cutting themselves off from village life — book low season (May–Oct) and the value improves clearly.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Every room sees the sea, but if you are paying for the view ask for a higher floor or a Sea View XL for an open outlook. · Walk out about 2 minutes to eat in the fishing village; the walking street is liveliest every Friday. · Book the Luxsa Spa and a seafront dinner at H Bistro on day one — they fill fast in peak season. · And booking May–Oct drops the rate noticeably.

entries.storyHtml: Bophut regulars have known NH Collection Samui Peace Resort for years under its old name, Peace Resort, before it joined Minor Hotels’ NH Collection and was renovated — a low-rise beachfront resort of 122 rooms, suites and villas spread through a beachside coconut garden, from garden bungalows to beachfront pool villas you can walk straight from onto the sand. It carries the biggest review base in this guide: 9.0 from 1,534 reviews on Booking.com. · Real guest reviews praise the warm, attentive staff as the reason people rebook, the spacious rooms stocked with extras, the large beachfront pool, and a fresh, varied breakfast buffet — all right on the beach yet about a 5-minute walk to the fishing village and only ~10 minutes from Samui airport. · Honest caveats: Bophut is shallow and the water pulls far out at low tide; storage in some rooms is tight; the resort is quiet at night with little in-house entertainment; and in-resort dining costs more than the shops outside. · Best for families and couples who want a quiet Bophut beach holiday at a friendlier price than a 5-star — book low season and walk out to eat in the village now and then to stretch the value.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Garden rooms are cheaper but don’t see the sea; for a sea wake-up choose Premier Ocean View or a beachfront pool villa and specify it when booking. · In-resort food is pricey — the 5-minute walk to Fisherman’s Village has plenty of options, and the Friday evening market is especially lively. · Check the tide times if you plan to swim, since Bophut is shallow.

entries.storyHtml: Walk the Bophut shore north from the fishing village until the noise fades and the garden turns green, and you reach Zazen Boutique Resort & Spa — a 4-star boutique of just 26 rooms and villas tucked into trees at the sand’s edge. The name comes from Japanese seated Zen meditation, and the whole resort is genuinely designed around it: Thai-Japanese style built for calm over size. It scores 9.0 from 294 reviews on Booking.com (TripAdvisor 4.7 from 1,600+ reviews, a Travelers’ Choice winner). · Real guest reviews praise the relaxing beachside garden, spacious spotless rooms and comfy beds, warm staff who make it right for special occasions, and the seafront restaurant The Club by Zazen — where island locals dine even without staying — with a bespoke Thai-dance show every Sunday night. · Honest caveats: the beach out front is narrow and shallow and awkward to enter at low tide; rooms and dining run on the pricey side; and rooms near the restaurant can hear music on Saturday and Sunday evenings. · Best for couples and honeymooners who want a small, quiet, romantic beachfront boutique — ask for an inner garden room if you are noise-sensitive, and book low season for a clearer rate.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: For space and privacy choose the ~65 sqm Garden Villa set deep in the garden. · Come on a Sunday evening for Thai Night’s dance show; Saturday is Glamour Night with a DJ. · Noise-sensitive? Ask for an inner garden room and avoid beachfront rooms near the restaurant. · Book the spa and a seafront table ahead in peak season.

entries.storyHtml: On the Fisherman’s Village walking street in Bophut — the old seafront lane that is among the liveliest after dark on Samui — a small boutique hides behind green foliage: Dreamcatcher Boutique Hotel (full name Dreamcatcher by Angelina). It scores 9.1 from 535 reviews on Booking.com at a start price around ฿1,400/night, the lowest in this guide. · What real guest reviews talk about is the boho design — no two rooms decorated alike, woven-bamboo ceilings, earth-toned polished plaster and dreamcatchers, from single-level rooms to duplex loft rooms that photograph beautifully — plus the Nomad rooftop bar for a sunset drink, and a location where you cross the road to the beach with restaurants and bars all around, only about 5 km from the airport. · Honest caveats: it is a 3-star boutique with no pool, stairs and no lift, right on a bar-lined street where some rooms hear music at night (especially Fri–Sat), and a few room types have weak air-con. · Best for couples, solo travellers and photographers who want a design stay in the middle of the village on a modest budget — ask for a quieter inner or upper AC room when you book.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: The hotel is on a bar street — ask for an inner or upper room and confirm it is an AC room when booking. · Try a duplex loft room with its mezzanine for great photos. · There is a water refill point, free snorkel gear and free sunscreen to borrow. · Rooms are few and fill fast Dec–Feb, so book ahead and pick Free Cancellation.

entries.storyHtml: Walk the Fisherman’s Village strip in Bophut at dusk and look up at the curved white Mediterranean building with a pool on its roof — that is Hacienda Fisherman’s Village, a small beachfront boutique in the middle of one of Samui’s liveliest strips, made up of the Hacienda and Hacienda Suite buildings a few steps apart on the seafront. Rooms start around ฿1,600/night; it scores 8.6 from real guest reviews (TripAdvisor 3.9 from 152 reviews). · The clear draw is the rooftop pool and solarium with views over Bophut Bay, the old fishing pier and the islands beyond — the sunset spot guests mention most — plus cute, clean rooms with Netflix TVs and private balconies, in a beachfront spot where you step out onto the walking street and the sand. · Honest caveats: it is a budget 3-star boutique with no lift (about 50 steps up to the top rooms and rooftop pool), a small pool better for a cool-off than laps, weak water pressure in some rooms, no parking on-site, and street-side rooms can hear the nightlife on weekends. · Best for couples and budget travellers who want a beachfront stay in the middle of the strip — pick a Sea View or an inner room to match what you want.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Go up to the rooftop pool at sunset — guests call it the unmissable highlight. · Want the sea? Choose a Sea View; want quiet? Ask for an inner or seaside room away from the street. · No lift, about 50 steps — ask for a lower floor if you have elderly guests or heavy bags. · Book with Free Cancellation and reconfirm with the hotel before you travel.

entries.storyHtml: Walk the Fisherman’s Village lane in Bophut to its far, seafront end, where the shops thin out and the noise drops, and you find GREENLIGHT Fisherman’s Village Resort — a small boutique that leans on green, calm and a self-roast coffee café rather than being a big hotel. It sits about 20 metres from the beach, another 2-minute walk to the shops and walking street, from around ฿4,000/night, scoring 8.9 from real guest reviews. · Real guest reviews praise the quiet-end location where you don’t hear the bars at night, the shady green garden with its garden pool, the GREENLIGHT Café roasting its own organic coffee with vegan/gluten-free options, friendly staff, and rooms bigger than expected for the price — only 3.4 km from Samui airport. · Honest caveats: it is a 3-star boutique with fewer facilities than a big resort, a small pool better for a cool-off than laps, limited rooms that book up in high season, and a still-small review base of 40 (which is why we place it in the back group despite the good score). · Best for travellers who want a small, quiet, friendly boutique within walking distance of beach and village — especially for a first or last night before flying out.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room facing the garden or pool for a nicer outlook than the inner rooms. · Try the fresh-roast coffee at GREENLIGHT Café in the morning before heading out. · At only 3.4 km from the airport it is ideal for a first or last night before flying home or catching a boat to another island. · Rooms are few Dec–Feb, so lock a Free Cancellation rate early.

entries.storyHtml: Most beachfront stays on Samui are big resorts of hundreds of rooms, but The Waterfront Boutique Hotel goes the other way — a small boutique of just 18 rooms right on Bophut Beach, where the owner lives locally and looks after guests personally. It is about a 3-minute walk to the shops and the Fisherman’s Village walking street, but sits on the quieter side; beachfront bungalows start around ฿3,000/night, scoring 8.4 from real guest reviews. · Real guest reviews praise the beachfront location and the warm, owner-run service that remembers guests, a pool facing the Gulf where you can watch the sunset with a pool bar, wide seafront bungalows many with direct sea views, and free bikes to borrow. · Honest caveats: it is a 3-star boutique whose building and furniture are starting to age, with some dated décor; the beach out front is shallow and silty at low tide, better for lounging than serious swimming; and facilities are simple, with no big spa or gym. · Best for travellers who want a small, friendly beachfront boutique at a reachable price — ask for a sea-facing bungalow when you book, and note only 18 rooms fill fast Dec–Feb.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a sea-facing bungalow for a better view and mood than the inner rooms. · Sit by the pool in the evening for the sunset and order from the pool bar. · Borrow a free bike to ride along Bophut Beach or into Fisherman’s Village. · Only 18 rooms, so lock a Free Cancellation rate early for Dec–Feb.

entries.storyHtml: Closing this guide is the highest-rated resort of the set — Anantara Bophut Koh Samui Resort, a 5-star Anantara (Minor Hotels) that chose Bophut on the island’s quieter, shadier north coast over busy Chaweng. The resort hides in a tropical garden of big trees and lotus ponds, 106 rooms and suites, many with private pools, from about ฿6,500/night, scoring 9.2 from real guest reviews — the highest here. · Real guest reviews praise the shady tropical garden and its privacy, the attentive Anantara service where staff remember you, the garden spa tucked behind lotus ponds, the beachfront infinity pool, and a location where a side gate puts you about 5 minutes from Fisherman’s Village and ~10 minutes from Samui airport. · Honest caveats: some entry-category rooms look more classic than the newly renovated ones, a few entry rooms have a garden rather than sea view, some back rooms hear road noise, and in-resort food and drink run on the pricey side. · Best for couples and families who want 5-star in a quiet garden setting while still being able to stroll the fishing village — upgrade to a Pool Suite if the budget allows, and ask for a beach-side room away from the road.

faqTitle: FAQ — common traveller questions about Bophut & Fisherman’s Village hotels, Koh Samui

faq.q: ❓ Which is the best hotel in Bophut & Fisherman’s Village?
faq.a: It depends on your trip and budget. By review score, Anantara Bophut at 9.2 — a 5-star garden resort — is the highest here. For 5-star right on the beach yet a 2-minute walk into the village, Hansar Samui at 9.1 is the flagship. The biggest review base and best value is NH Collection Samui Peace Resort at 9.0 from 1,534 reviews. On a modest budget in the middle of the walking street, Dreamcatcher scores 9.1 from about ฿1,400.

faq.q: ❓ How much do Bophut hotels cost?
faq.a: In this guide, prices start from about ฿1,400–8,000 per night. The budget end is Dreamcatcher from ฿1,400 and Hacienda from ฿1,600 (walking-street boutiques). Mid-range is The Waterfront ฿3,000, GREENLIGHT ฿4,000, NH Collection Peace ฿4,500 and Zazen ฿5,500. The luxury end is Anantara Bophut from ฿6,500 and Hansar from ฿8,000. All are approximate starting rates outside peak; high season (December–February) rises clearly.

faq.q: ❓ How is Bophut / Fisherman’s Village different from Chaweng, and who is it for?
faq.a: Bophut is a beach on the island’s north coast, much quieter than Chaweng, with Fisherman’s Village at its heart — an old seafront lane turned into restaurants, bars, cafés and a Friday walking-street market. The beach is shallow and pulls far out at low tide, so it suits relaxing and strolling. Chaweng, by contrast, is the hub of the action, with wide white sand and lots of nightlife. Bophut suits couples, families and anyone who wants a quiet beach that still has food and things to do within walking distance, only about 10 minutes from the airport. If you want all-day swimming and heavy nightlife, Chaweng fits better.

faq.q: ❓ Which hotels here can you walk to the beach and the walking street from?
faq.a: Right on the walking street are Dreamcatcher and Hacienda — cross the road to the beach with shops all around. Beachfront with a short walk to the village are Hansar (2 min), NH Collection Peace (~5 min) and The Waterfront (3 min). GREENLIGHT sits at the quiet end of the village, a 2-minute walk to the strip but calm at night. Zazen (~20 min) and Anantara (~5 min) are set back in the garden zone, quieter and more private.

faq.q: ❓ Can you swim at Bophut Beach?
faq.a: Bophut is a shallow beach where the water pulls far out at low tide, and some stretches have natural seaweed or silt — it suits lounging on the sand and watching the sky more than serious swimming. If you plan to swim, check the tide times and go in at high tide, or use your hotel’s pool. For real all-day white-sand swimming, hop over to Chaweng or a wider beach now and then.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should you book, and how do you get around?
faq.a: For Koh Samui high season (December–February, plus July–August, book 1–2 months ahead), especially small stays like The Waterfront (18 rooms) and GREENLIGHT, which fill first. In low season, 1–2 weeks ahead is fine and rates drop noticeably. Getting there: Bophut is only about 10 minutes from Samui airport, with hotel cars, taxis and Grab. Every platform offers Free Cancellation, so lock a rate if your plans aren’t firm, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
